method_notes: All current prices fetched 2026-10-11 between ~22:15 and ~23:05 UTC with WebFetch on the public APIs, using a dummy cache-busting query parameter (&cb=<n>).

Important: un-busted API URLs returned stale cached snapshots (e.g., a Kalshi trades call returned trades from 2026-10-02; several event calls showed lower cumulative volume and prices up to 4 points different). Live pages should fetch directly from the browser, not through a caching proxy.
Kalshi API now returns prices as *_dollars strings (0-1) and sizes as *_fp; the older integer-cent fields (last_price, yes_bid, yes_ask, volume) are no longer present.

Polymarket CLOB (clob.polymarket.com) and PredictIt (predictit.org) could not be fetched in this session (domain permission not granted), so Polymarket price history is missing and PredictIt figures come only from ElectionBettingOdds.com.

Senate-control rules by venue. Polymarket: independents who caucus, or announce they will caucus, with a party count for it; undetermined caucusing can hold the market open until Jan 4, 2027, after which such a member counts for no party; with no majority, control goes to the party holding half the seats plus the Vice Presidency (Republican under VP Vance), else the party of the first President pro tempore. Kalshi CONTROLS: consensus media call, else the party of the President pro tempore on Feb 1, 2027. Kalshi seat-count contracts count caucusing independents with their party. Nebraska: Polymarket prices Osborn only through 'Will an independent win...?' (party markets exclude independents); Kalshi has a separate SENATENE-26-DOSB contract ('Dan Osborn (as an independent)'). PredictIt rules: not obtained.

p definitions. Polymarket p = Gamma outcomePrices[0]. Kalshi p = (yes_bid+yes_ask)/2. PredictIt/Betfair p = midpoint of the bid-ask range shown on ElectionBettingOdds.com. Kalshi volume and open interest are in contracts with a $1 payout; aggregators such as ElectionBettingOdds report the contract count as dollars.

studies.finding: Iowa Electronic Markets vote-share prices were closer to the eventual two-party vote split than 964 polls 74% of the time across five presidential elections (1988-2004).
studies.source: Berg, Nelson & Rietz, 'Prediction market accuracy in the long run', International Journal of Forecasting 24(2): 285-300

studies.finding: When poll leads are properly discounted for their typical shift before Election Day, poll-based forecasts outperform IEM vote-share prices, and winner-take-all market prices were less accurate than poll-based win probabilities.
studies.source: Erikson & Wlezien, 'Are Political Markets Really Superior to Polls as Election Predictors?', Public Opinion Quarterly 72(2): 190-215 (doi:10.1093/poq/nfn010)

studies.finding: After debiasing both, prediction-market-based forecasts gave more accurate probabilities of victory than poll-based forecasts, especially early in the cycle and in uncertain races.
studies.source: Rothschild, 'Forecasting Elections: Comparing Prediction Markets, Polls, and Their Biases', Public Opinion Quarterly 73(5): 895-916 (doi:10.1093/poq/nfp082)

studies.finding: Prediction markets are reasonably well calibrated close to expiration, but prices for events farther in the future show a favourite-longshot bias (likely events underpriced, unlikely events overpriced).
studies.source: Page & Clemen, 'Do Prediction Markets Produce Well-Calibrated Probability Forecasts?', Economic Journal 123(568): 491-513 (doi:10.1111/j.1468-0297.2012.02561.x)

studies.finding: In ~2,500 markets (~$2.5B volume) in the final five weeks of the 2024 election, the share of markets whose favorite matched the outcome was 67% on Polymarket, 78% on Kalshi and 93% on PredictIt; prices were weakly correlated across exchanges and 58% of Polymarket national presidential markets showed negative serial correlation. Kalshi disputed the methodology.
studies.source: Clinton & Huang (Vanderbilt University) working paper, as reported by DL News, 5 Dec 2025 (not yet peer-reviewed)

studies.finding: Across 292 million trades on 327,000 Kalshi and Polymarket contracts, political markets showed persistent underconfidence, with prices 'chronically compressed toward 50%'.
studies.source: Le, 'Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics in Prediction Markets', arXiv:2602.19520 (preprint, Feb 2026)

landscape.fact: Polymarket settled with the CFTC (US$1.4 million fine) for offering unregistered contracts and restricted U.S. access.
Judge Jia M. Cobb (U.S. District Court for D.C.) ruled the CFTC exceeded its authority in blocking Kalshi's congressional-control contracts.
D.C. Circuit Judge Patricia Millett denied the CFTC's motion for a stay pending appeal, allowing Kalshi to list election contracts.
A French trader ('Théo') placed about $30 million on Trump via several Polymarket accounts; the WSJ reported his bets skewed the odds and raised manipulation fears.

The D.C. Circuit granted the CFTC's unopposed motion (filed 5 May 2025) to drop its appeal, leaving the ruling for Kalshi in place; Kalshi said it had over $500 million in volume on its presidential markets.
X named Polymarket its official prediction market partner, with a joint product combining Polymarket data, X posts and Grok annotations.
Polymarket acquired CFTC-licensed exchange QCEX to return to the U.S.; the U.S. product opened to waitlisted customers in December 2025.
Google Finance announced it would integrate Kalshi and Polymarket prediction-market data.
CNN named Kalshi its official prediction markets partner.
landscape.source: The Block, 4 Dec 2025 (referencing a 2 Dec 2025 announcement)

landscape.fact: CNBC signed an exclusive deal to use Kalshi data across TV, digital and subscription products starting in 2026. The article said Kalshi and Polymarket had combined 2025 volume above $45 billion and Kalshi was valued at $11 billion after a $1 billion raise.
Kalshi and Polymarket both showed Democrats about 51% to win the Senate, the first time Democrats were favored on Kalshi's contract. The article tied the move to escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.

Kalshi fined three congressional candidates for betting on their own races and suspended them for five years: Mark Moran (>$6,200), Zeke Enriquez (>$780) and Matt Klein (>$530). Rep. Mike Levin called it 'a parking ticket'. In March, Kalshi and Polymarket had banned candidates from trading on their own campaigns.
Polymarket's U.S. iOS app opened to everyone on the waitlist; no access code is needed.
After a NYT/Siena poll, Kalshi priced a GOP Senate at 60% ($7.5M volume) and Polymarket at 57% ($2.8M).

Through 10 Aug 2026, $133M had been wagered on 2026 congressional races, versus $92M in the whole 2024 cycle. Kalshi had about $93M and Polymarket US about 15% of Kalshi's volume. There were 7,466 markets (vs 463 in 2024), the top 1% of Polymarket wallets held 68% of volume, and ACDC projected $1.4-1.6B in total.
landscape.source: Reuters via GV Wire; Anti-Corruption Data Collective briefing

Kalshi disclosed further insider cases, including a NC House nominee fined about $2,600. Some counties have adopted bans on election trading.
